interactions.label: A positive urinary hCG test is classified as a positive sign of pregnancy becaus

params.question: A positive urinary hCG test is classified as a positive sign of pregnancy because it confirms the presence of a foetus.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Despite its name, a 'positive' pregnancy test is only a probable sign of pregnancy. Ectopic pregnancies and gestational trophoblastic disease can give a positive result without an intrauterine foetus. Only foetal heart sounds, examiner-felt movements, and ultrasound visualisation qualify as positive (diagnostic) signs.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A positive hCG test is only a probable sign. Ectopic pregnancies and gestational trophoblastic disease can produce a positive hCG result without an intrauterine foetus. True positive signs require direct evidence of the foetus — foetal heart sounds, examiner-felt foetal movements, or ultrasound visualisation.

interactions.label: Why is a man NOT considered sterile immediately after a vasectomy?

params.question: Why is a man NOT considered sterile immediately after a vasectomy?

answers.text: The vas deferens may spontaneously recanalise within the first month

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Recanalisation is a rare long-term complication, not the reason for the waiting period after vasectomy.

answers.text: Residual sperm remain in the reproductive tract distal to the ligation site

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Sperm already in the tract beyond the ligation point can still be ejaculated. Azoospermia must be confirmed by semen analysis at twelve weeks.

answers.text: Testosterone levels take several weeks to decline sufficiently

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Vasectomy does not affect testosterone production — it only interrupts sperm transport through the vas deferens.

answers.text: The epididymis continues to release mature sperm into the bloodstream

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sperm are not released into the bloodstream after vasectomy. They remain in the ductal system until cleared by ejaculation.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key point is that sperm already present beyond the vasectomy site remain viable for several weeks. Semen analysis at twelve weeks must confirm azoospermia before the man can rely on the vasectomy for contraception.
Exactly right. The twelve-week semen analysis confirming azoospermia is a critical step — failing to explain this during consent counselling can lead to negligence claims if a pregnancy occurs.

interactions.label: At autopsy, a young woman who died after a suspected criminal abortion shows che

params.question: At autopsy, a young woman who died after a suspected criminal abortion shows chemical peritonitis and frothy blood in the right heart chambers. Which method of criminal abortion best explains these findings?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Oral quinine causes gastric mucosal irritation and drug traces at autopsy, not chemical peritonitis or air embolism.
Incorrect. Unsterile instruments cause cervical lacerations and uterine perforation — a mechanical injury pattern, not a chemical one.

answers.text: Intrauterine introduction of soap solution or lysol

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Caustic fluids introduced into the uterus cause chemical peritonitis, and the procedure can introduce air into the uterine veins, producing a fatal air embolism visible as frothy blood in the heart chambers.
Incorrect. Oral misoprostol produces drug traces and gastric findings at autopsy, but not chemical peritonitis from a caustic agent.

overallFeedback.feedback: Chemical peritonitis points to a caustic agent (soap solution, lysol) introduced into the uterus. Frothy blood in the heart chambers indicates air embolism — air entering the uterine veins during the procedure. Together, these are the hallmark of caustic-fluid criminal abortion.
Well done. Recognising the combination of chemical peritonitis plus air embolism as the signature of intrauterine caustic fluids is a key forensic skill in criminal abortion cases.

interactions.label: Under the PC&PNDT Act, which of the following is mandatory for every antenatal u

params.question: Under the PC&PNDT Act, which of the following is mandatory for every antenatal ultrasound performed at a registered facility?

answers.text: Prior written approval from the District Magistrate for each scan

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Registration with the Appropriate Authority is mandatory for the facility, but individual scans do not require prior approval from the District Magistrate.

answers.text: Completion of Form F with records maintained for two years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Every antenatal ultrasound requires a completed Form F, and the records must be maintained for two years — a key compliance requirement under the PC&PNDT Act.

answers.text: Mandatory referral to a government genetic counselling centre

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The Act regulates genetic counselling centres but does not require referral to a government centre for every ultrasound.

answers.text: Reporting the foetal sex to the Appropriate Authority within 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Disclosing the foetal sex is strictly prohibited under the Act — it may not be communicated to anyone, including any authority.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Act mandates that every antenatal ultrasound is accompanied by a completed Form F, and records must be kept for two years. Disclosing the foetal sex — to anyone — is strictly prohibited.
Correct. Form F documentation and two-year record retention are among the most frequently examined provisions of the PC&PNDT Act.

interactions.label: An apparently healthy 3-month-old infant is found dead in the prone position on

params.question: An apparently healthy 3-month-old infant is found dead in the prone position on soft bedding. Autopsy reveals only thymic petechiae and pulmonary congestion. What must the forensic pathologist do before concluding this death is SIDS?

answers.text: Order toxicology screening and conclude SIDS if the results are negative

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Toxicology is part of a complete autopsy, but a negative result alone is insufficient. A thorough death scene investigation and clinical history review are also required.

answers.text: Conduct a thorough death scene investigation and review all prior medical records

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. SIDS is a diagnosis of exclusion. It requires a full autopsy, a death scene investigation (sleeping position, bedding, co-sleepers, surveillance footage), and a review of the clinical history — all three must fail to identify a cause before SIDS can be concluded.

answers.text: Perform histological examination of the thymus to confirm the diagnosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Thymic petechiae are nonspecific findings that can occur in both SIDS and smothering. No single autopsy finding confirms SIDS.

answers.text: Attribute the death to positional asphyxia based on the prone sleeping position

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Prone sleeping is a risk factor for SIDS, not proof of positional asphyxia. Concluding a cause of death without a complete investigation is premature and may miss a homicide.

overallFeedback.feedback: SIDS is a diagnosis of exclusion requiring three components: a full autopsy, a thorough death scene investigation, and a review of the clinical history. Autopsy findings alone — especially nonspecific ones like thymic petechiae — cannot distinguish SIDS from homicidal smothering.

Exactly right. SIDS is diagnosed only when autopsy, scene investigation, and clinical history review all fail to identify a cause — this is critical because homicidal smothering can look virtually identical at autopsy.
